plan.summary: This 1-4 block is a simple off-camp boxing S&C build with one weekly session, so the plan keeps the highest-value work only: explosive throws and jumps first, then basic strength, then trunk and brief conditioning. Week 1 establishes training maxes for the main lower-body lift so percentage work can start in Week 2. With only one lifting day per week and a boxing preference for extra conditioning, the plan uses conservative strength volume and finishes with short, practical conditioning that supports the sport without beating up recovery.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general lower-body power, squat strength, trunk stiffness, and basic conditioning with simple repeatable work.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the main strength and power work while keeping the total session compact and recoverable around boxing practice.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Shift toward faster, sharper outputs while keeping enough strength work to hold onto the force gains.

exercises.name: 1a. Medicine Ball Chest Pass
exercises.notes: Throw every rep fast from a stable stance. Reset between reps and use a non-bouncing ball or catch dead against a wall.

substitutionOptions.name: Explosive Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if no medicine ball is available. Keep reps crisp and stop before speed drops.

exercises.name: 1b. Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can with a quiet landing. Full reset between reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low safe box and step down each rep.

exercises.name: 2. Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up progressively, then work up to your hardest clean set of 3-5 reps. Keep the torso tall and stop if depth or control breaks. This session sets your starting reference for future loading.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can estimate your working max for the next weeks.

substitutionOptions.name: Double Dumbbell Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if the kettlebell or dumbbell is too light for a meaningful test.

exercises.name: 3a. One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Pull to the hip, pause briefly, and keep the torso still. Work at a smooth RPE 7-8.

substitutionOptions.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if lower-back support is needed.

exercises.name: 3b. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Leave 1-2 reps in reserve and keep the body straight. Elevate the hands if needed to keep clean reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if wrist comfort or shoulder position makes push-ups awkward.

exercises.name: 4. Suitcase Carry
exercises.notes: Walk tall without leaning. Use a load that challenges the trunk but does not pull you out of position.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Rack Carry
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if space is limited and short shuttle lengths are needed.

exercises.name: 5. Conditioning Finisher
exercises.notes: Keep the pace steady and nasal-breathing if possible. This should build fitness without trashing your legs for boxing.

endurancePrescription.structure: Choose jump rope, shadowboxing rounds, or brisk uphill walking if available.
